newsitem.title: USA: Ex-developer sentenced to five years for bribery.
newsitem.headline: Ex-developer sentenced to five years for bribery.

text.p: A federal judge in Chicago has sentenced a former Illinois developer to more than five years in federal prison for bribing a suburban official to obtain city-backed bond financing for his construction plans.

U.S. District Judge John Grady also leveled nearly $10 million of fines, forfeitures and restitution against Robert Krilich in sentencing him Monday, said Randall Samborn, spokesman for U.S. Attorney Jim Burns.

Krilich, 66, had been convicted in 1995 of repeatedly bribing former Oak Brook Terrace Mayor Richard Sarallo. Sarallo pleaded guilty to tax evasion and was sentenced to six months in prison but denied taking bribes.
The bribery schemes included a rigged hole-in-one contest in 1985 won by a son of Sarallo's, who won a $40,000 car.

Krilich could have been sentenced to more than 12 years in prison, but Grady sentenced him to 64 months in prison, ordered him to forfeit $8.67 million in assets, fined him $1 million and mandated $40,000 of restitution to the insurer of the hole-in-one contest.
